subject: Decision requested: Legacy v1 bridge for Orchard Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-09-30T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Decision requested: Legacy v1 bridge for Orchard Health

Team —

Orchard Health (HIPAA customer) just asked to keep our older v1 model endpoint (text-generate-v1) available for an additional 6 months. Their compliance team is mid-validation and cannot certify the new v2-based flow until November; switching now would block a major go-live scheduled for Jan. They asked for a documented "legacy bridge" and an SLA commitment for the older endpoint during that period.

Quick context: this is an expansion (D-8241) and they are greenlit if we can provide a stable path without breaking existing JSON schemas. Product wants to know operational/tech tradeoffs and whether we can offer a limited contract addendum instead of a permanent exemption. I attached the customer's migration_timeline.xlsx that they shared.

Asks (please):
- Ben: can we keep v1 running behind a compatibility shim? If so, cost and risk summary (security surface, maintenance) and a concise one-liner we can share with Legal/CS.
- Priyom: ops impact, capacity needs, and how long lead time to stand up a ring with reserved capacity (Dedicated/Private) for this customer. Include any billing implications.
- Evelyn: product POV on feature/regression risk and whether we can promise compatibility without blocking v2 improvements.

Goal: firm decision by Friday EOD (2026-10-02) so I can send a clear commitment to the customer and attach to the contract amendment. If we agree to a temporary bridge, we also need comm wording and an internal stop-gap plan (monitoring, sunset date, rollback plan).

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Platform Partnerships | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
[Attachment: migration_timeline.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Decision requested: Legacy v1 bridge for Orchard Health

Marissa —

Short answer: yes, technically feasible, but non-trivial. Notes: 
- v1 uses legacy KV cache layout and older attention-kernel paths that we removed from our mainline docker images last quarter. Running both means keeping a separate runtime image (or runtime flag) and a compatibility shim layer to translate current request/response envelopes to the old schema.
- Surface area: increased test matrix, extra perf regressions to watch (esp. long-sequence tails), and additional SLO obligations for two runtime families.

Estimated incremental cost (engineering + infra) for a 6-month bridge: approx 0.7 FTE eng overhead (maintenance/safety), + ongoing infra delta of ~$12k/mo if we reserve Dedicated capacity for them. If we do a per-request shim without Dedicated, expect higher latency and per-token costs. I attached a short cost estimate.

Mitigation option: implement a focused compatibility shim that sits in front of v2 for the Orchard tenant only. That would translate v1 payloads to v2, run with v2 kernels, and translate output back. Pros: less runtime variance, can leverage v2 kernels. Cons: risk of subtle behavioral drift and additional acceptance testing.

My recommended ask to Legal/Product: allow a timeboxed (90-180 day) bridge with explicit sunset and a requirement for Orchard to validate against our acceptance test-suite. We should add heightened QA gating (automated prompt-set checks) before enabling the shim.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
[Attachment: shim-cost-estimate.pdf (pdf)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Decision requested: Legacy v1 bridge for Orchard Health

Marissa —

Operations notes: we can provision a dedicated canary lane for Orchard in Dedicated or isolate via tenancy on our shared pool. Timeline and constraints: 
- Dedicated reserved pool: 2–3 week lead time to provision nodes and network entitlements; requires a minimum monthly commit (depends on region) — ops needs sign-off on billing change.
- Shared pool shim: near-immediate but risk of noisy neighbors; to meet their SLA request we'd need to add auto-scaling headroom which increases cost.

For billing: recommend a short-term addendum that includes a monthly dedicated fee (we can bake it into D-8241); alternatively charge for support/maintenance as a separate line item. If Legal wants an SLA on the legacy endpoint, ops requires a 30% uplift on the baseline reserve to meet percentile latency targets.

I can draft operational runbook and capacity provisioning checklist; will need the final sunset date and acceptance criteria to size alerts and runbooks.

Priyom
Priyom Das
Head of Product Operations | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T16:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Decision requested: Legacy v1 bridge for Orchard Health

All —

Product perspective: extended maintenance of v1 constrains our ability to ship v2 improvements that change output shape (tokenization, structured fields). To limit long-term drag, product supports a timeboxed bridge but with these conditions: 
- Sunset at 2027-03-15 (135 days) unless Orchard signs an extended support contract.
- Oracle acceptance: Orchard must run our regression test-suite (we'll provide the test vectors) and sign off on any semantic acceptability deviations.
- No major model-architecture changes to the v1 translation shim during the bridge window; any fixes must go through a hardened review.

I created a short comm draft in Notion with suggested wording for the customer and internal escalation steps. Link: https://www.notion.so/redwood/Orchard-Legacy-Bridge-Decision-7f6a1b2c

If we approve this, Product will also cut a small QE sprint to validate the shim before we flip it on. That adds ~2 weeks to Ben's timeline if we go the shim route.

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Product Management | Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helen Liu <helen.liu@orchardhealth.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@orchardhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T18:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Decision requested: Legacy v1 bridge for Orchard Health

Team —

Thank you all for fast turnarounds. Per the notes above, here is my proposed internal decision and the customer wording. Please flag any factual errors by EOD Friday. If silent, I'll send this to Orchard Legal and CS and start the provisioning + contract amendment flow.

INTERNAL DECISION SUMMARY (proposed):
- APPROVE: timeboxed legacy bridge for Orchard Health for 135 days (sunset 2027-03-15).
- CONDITION: Orchard must run and sign off on Redwood's acceptance test-suite; bridge enabled only after QE signoff.
- BILLING: Dedicated reserved lane with +30% capacity uplift; include $12k/mo infra delta in amendment.
- MONITORING: Add prompt-set regression checks and elevated alerts (Product + SRE owners).

CUSTOMER COMMUNICATION (PROPOSED EMAIL TO ORCHARD):
Hi Helen / Samir —

Thanks for the context and for sharing your validation timeline. We can accommodate a timeboxed legacy bridge to keep your existing v1 endpoint active while you complete certification. High level: we will enable a tenant-specific compatibility bridge, subject to acceptance testing and a written amendment to your contract. The bridge will be active until 2027-03-15 unless extended by mutual agreement. There will be a dedicated capacity uplift and a monthly infrastructure fee outlined in the amendment. We'll share the acceptance test-suite and a short runbook.

Next steps:
1) If you agree to acceptance testing, please confirm by COB next Wed (2026-10-06).
2) Legal can review our amendment (we'll circulate a draft once we get internal approval).
3) Ops will confirm provisioning ETA after contract sign-off.

If that reads correctly, I'll send this version to Orchard and loop Legal.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Platform Partnerships | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
